principle_text: When a persuadee expresses interest but cites personal constraints preventing donation, avoid pushing for immediate contributions and instead focus on building rapport and understanding their situation.
When the persuadee responds to vague or unrelated statements, avoid making comments that do not clearly connect to the donation goal or provide compelling reasons to donate.
When the persuadee focuses on political controversies without linking them to the charitable cause, avoid merely acknowledging the topic without steering the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee expresses a negative or uncertain opinion about a topic, avoid making assumptions about their preferences that may cause disagreement or distract from the donation goal.
When the persuadee expresses curiosity about your opinions, avoid simply stating agreement without providing reasons that connect to the donation goal.
When the persuadee shows interest in reasons behind opinions, avoid making highly charged or divisive comparisons that shift focus away from the charitable donation topic.
When the persuadee expresses strong opinions on unrelated political topics, avoid continuing the political discussion to prevent distraction from the charitable donation goal.
When the persuadee expresses opinions unrelated to the donation goal, avoid vague or open-ended questions that do not guide the conversation toward charitable giving.
When the persuadee expresses agreement but concludes the conversation politely without mentioning donation, avoid simply agreeing without guiding the discussion toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee expresses financial hardship and doubts their ability to help, avoid focusing on your own struggles without clearly connecting how small contributions can still make an impact.
When the persuadee expresses financial hardship and uncertainty about their impact, avoid introducing abstract concepts that do not clearly connect to motivating donation behavior.
When the persuadee expresses financial hardship and prioritizes essential needs, avoid asking directly for donations from their limited funds as it may lead to immediate refusal.
When a persuadee expresses financial constraints but shows some openness, you should introduce matching donations as an incentive to increase their engagement and willingness to contribute.
When the persuadee shows concern but hesitates to donate, you should introduce specific, emotional examples to increase empathy and engagement toward charitable giving.
When the persuadee expresses concern about limited funds, you should offer a matching donation incentive and mention a reputable charity to increase engagement and encourage contribution.
When the persuadee expresses hesitation about donation amounts, avoid applying pressure that could cause discomfort or resistance without offering additional motivation.
When the persuadee feels limited by their financial capacity, you should emphasize that even small donations can make a meaningful difference to encourage their willingness to contribute.
When a persuadee expresses willingness to help despite limited resources, you should emphasize that any contribution, no matter how small, can make a meaningful difference and personalize the appeal.
When the persuadee expresses financial constraints, avoid pushing for higher donation amounts that may discourage their willingness to contribute.
When a persuadee offers a smaller donation than requested, you should positively reinforce their willingness to contribute to encourage a supportive and affirming atmosphere.
When the persuadee expresses hope or positive sentiment without clear commitment, avoid brief acknowledgments that miss opportunities to reinforce or deepen their engagement.
When the persuadee expresses hope or agreement with the cause, avoid giving minimal or non-committal responses that do not reinforce or deepen their commitment to donate.

When the persuadee expresses willingness to help and positive feelings about the cause, you should reinforce their attitude by sharing your own commitment and framing donation as being part of the solution.
When the persuadee expresses willingness to help but does not immediately respond to increased donation requests, avoid pressing too directly for higher amounts without gauging their readiness.
